reference.title: Console settings, environment variables and the secret key
reference.shortdesc: Which settings the admin console stores, how environment variables override them, how changes reach every service, and how stored secrets are protected.

section.title: Environment variables win
section.p: Each group of settings comes from its environment variables when they are set, and from the admin console otherwise. A group never mixes the two: setting OIDC_ISSUER replaces the whole OIDC setup stored in the console. The console shows such a group as Set by environment, read-only; remove the variables to manage it in the console.

strow.stentry: GITHUB_APP_ID and GITHUB_APP_PRIVATE_KEY, or OPEND_GITHUB_BROKER_URL (managed hosting)
Only ever on where OPEND_DEV_LOGIN allows them; the console can turn them off

section.p: Site access, the docs repository, organizations and readers live in their own tables, as before, and the admin API changes the same records.

section.title: Changes apply without a restart
section.p: Every change sends a Postgres notification. The web service (every replica), the worker and the editor reload their settings when it arrives, and re-read them at least once a minute in case a notification is missed. Sign-in providers are rebuilt only when their own settings change.

section.title: The secret key
section.p: Client secrets, the GitHub App's private key and its webhook secret are sealed with AES-256-GCM before they reach the database, bound to their names so one cannot be swapped for another. No page, API route, log line or audit entry ever contains one; the console only says whether each is set.

The key comes from OPEND_SECRET_KEY when it is set. Otherwise it is derived from SESSION_SECRET with HKDF under a label of its own, so it is never the session key itself. Either way, every service that reads the settings needs the same value: give the worker and the editor the web service's SESSION_SECRET (or OPEND_SECRET_KEY).
section.note: Without OPEND_SECRET_KEY, changing SESSION_SECRET makes the stored secrets unreadable. Nothing breaks silently: the console warns about them, and the settings behave as if unset until you enter the client secret again or reconnect GitHub. Set OPEND_SECRET_KEY before you store secrets if you rotate session secrets.
